name: Pewter Blue
lede: Pewter Blue is a cool grey-blue named for pewter, the dull metal alloy, but who first paired the two words as a color name is undocumented in the sources consulted here.

sections.title: A metal's name, undocumented coining
sections.body:
Our color library carries this name only through a plain wiki-sourced list entry, with no dated plate, dictionary or survey behind it [1]. Pewter is a dull-grey tin alloy long used for tableware, and the pairing with "blue" describes the cool, muted cast of this particular grey-blue [1]. Who first used the combined name for this exact swatch is undocumented in our sources [1].

The nearest named colors by measured distance are [[ethereal-blue]] and [[grey-blue]], both almost the same shade [2]. [[watteau]], [[russian-blue]], [[cadet-grey]] and [[greyish-blue]] sit a little further out, all bluer [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive of 23,781 paintings finds a match for this grey-blue in 334 of them, about 1.4 percent, more common than 71 percent of the named colors we track, as photographed [3]. It peaks in the 1900s, at 2.1 times the expected rate for that century (31 of 1,674 paintings from then), and inside a painting it most often plays a light passage, in 41 percent of its matches, ranked by lightness rather than raw area [3]. Alfred Sisley is its most devoted painter here, using it in 7 of 50 works, 7.4 times the baseline for the museums those works come from [3]. The earliest match is dated 1467; our archive's early centuries are thin, so that date is a floor, not a first [3].
